use /ui
from /scope/prompt-mode import PromptEditor

export ui-component Planning:
    pitch:
        A plain, quick list of the work still to do, as Linear keeps issues:
        stories written ahead of time, each saying how it will be sent, Code,
        Chain, Spec, Ask, or Freeform, gathered into the next sprint and sent
        to the agent in order, all at once.

    description:
        Planning opens in a tab of its own in the body, "Planning", with a
        checklist icon, as a file opens, as the @{Body} says, from the
        ribbon's Planning tab or the palette's "Planning". It is one column
        of stories, at most 760 pixels wide, centred, in two sections, each
        headed by its name and count: "Next sprint", at the top, and
        "Backlog", beneath it. A section with nothing in it reads, muted,
        "Nothing planned" or "Backlog is empty".

    stories:
        A story is one piece of work, written as it will be sent: a title,
        a prompt, and how it will be sent. Each is a row, 36 pixels tall: a
        drag grip at its left; a small mode picker, a pill reading its mode,
        "Code", "Chain", "Spec", "Ask", or "Freeform", in that mode's colour,
        as the @{PromptModes} colours it; its title, in the body's text
        colour, cut off with an ellipsis; then, at its right, muted, a small
        icon for anything attached, and, once it has been sent, its status
        as a task's is shown. Hovering a row shows a menu button at its
        right. A story has no Send of its own, as the sprint says.

        Clicking a row opens it beneath, expanded in place, the others
        moving down: its title, editable in place; its prompt, in a
        @{GrowingTextInput} with the chat input's highlighting, completions,
        and slicing, as the @{ChatInput} has, and its attachments beneath;
        and its parameters, its mode, model, effort, and Slice, as the chat
        input shows them. Every change is saved as it is made. Only one
        story is open at a time; Escape or clicking its row again closes
        it.

    creating:
        Creating a story is quick. A "New story" line at the foot of Next
        sprint, and Ctrl+N (Cmd+N on macOS) while Planning has focus, adds a
        story at the end of Next sprint, open, its title focused, in the mode
        last picked for a story. However a story is added, it goes into Next
        sprint, at its end: a new story, a duplicate, an accepted proposal
        for a new story, and one added from an Ask answer's card alike. It
        can then be moved to the Backlog to wait, as the sprint says. Typing a title and pressing Enter adds it and starts another
        beneath it, so a list can be written down without the mouse; Escape
        on an empty one removes it. A title with no prompt sends its title as
        its prompt.

        A story can also be prompted into existence: "Draft stories", a
        button beside the Backlog's heading, opens a small box to say what is
        wanted, in a sentence or a paragraph, and asks the harness, in a run
        of its own with no session, with the planning prompt of the
        @{BakedSystemPrompts}, to break it into stories, each with a title, a
        prompt, and the mode that fits it. They come back as proposals, as
        the drafting and proposals say, each to be accepted, edited, or
        rejected, and none reaches the plan until it is accepted. An Ask
        answer's prompt cards also offer "Add to sprint", which adds the
        card's prompt as a story in its mode to Next sprint.

    sprint:
        Stories move between the Backlog and Next sprint by dragging, as the
        @{DragReorderBehaviour} says, across the sections as within them, or
        from a row's menu, "Move to next sprint" or "Move to backlog". Their
        order within Next sprint is the order they will be sent. A row's menu
        also has "Duplicate" and "Delete".

        "Send sprint", a primary button at the right of Next sprint's
        heading, enabled while it holds a story, sends every story in it, in
        order, as though each had been written in the chat input on its
        mode's tab and sent, one after another, as the @{PromptSending} says:
        each task queues in its lane behind the one before it, in the order
        of the sprint, and each question runs at once. The stories go into
        the queue as one block, so nothing sent later comes between them,
        and the queue's auto-send carries them on as ever, as the
        @{QueueList} says. A story's own "Send" sends it alone the same way.

        A story once sent stays in its section, its row showing its task's
        status as it queues, runs, and ends, and clicking it opens its task
        in the Tasks tab. Once every story of the sprint has ended, the
        section offers "Close sprint", which moves the stories that are done
        into a muted, collapsed "Done" list beneath the Backlog, and leaves
        any that failed or were cancelled in Next sprint, to be sent again.

    saving:
        The stories, their order, and which section each is in are saved
        with the project's data, as the @{ProjectData} says, in
        `.suspense/planning/`, a file per story, holding its hidden anchor
        as a queued prompt's is, and an `order.json` listing the sections and
        their stories, so the plan is kept with the project and comes back
        as it was left. A story's steps are saved in its own file, in their
        order, as its steps say, never apart from it.

    steps:
        A story can have steps: one or more further prompts, each a piece of
        the story done after the one before, as a chain's steps are. Each
        step has a prompt, a mode of its own, Code or Spec, starting as the
        story's, and a model and effort, starting as the story's, and may
        have attachments. A story with no steps is just its own prompt, as
        before; its prompt is always its first step.

        An open story lists its steps beneath its prompt, in order, each a
        row numbered from 2, the story's own prompt being 1, with its mode
        pill and the first line of its prompt, opening in place to edit, as
        a story does. "Add step", beneath the last, adds one at the end,
        open and focused; several can be added one after another, Enter in
        an empty step's prompt adding none. Steps are reordered by dragging,
        as the @{DragReorderBehaviour} says, or Alt+Up and Alt+Down, and each
        has a remove button in its row and in its menu. The story's own
        prompt stays first and can't be moved among them.

        A step belongs to its story and to nothing else. It is saved in the
        story's file, in a `steps` list of the story's hidden anchor, in its
        order, and saved as every change to the plan is, straight away; a
        story duplicated copies its steps, and one deleted deletes them. Its
        order is kept wherever the story goes, between sections, into a
        sprint, and back from Done.

        Wherever the story is shown, its steps are too: its row in Planning
        shows how many after its title, muted, as "3 steps", with the list in
        its tooltip; the open story lists them as above; a proposal to add
        to it shows them, so what it would add to can be seen; and once it
        is sent, it is sent as a chain, its prompt first and each step after
        it in order, each step sent only once the one before it finishes, as
        the @{PromptEditor}'s chained tasks are, so the Tasks tab shows the
        story as one chain with its steps beneath it. A story sent can't be
        given more steps; its steps, sent or still to come, read as they
        were sent.

        A step is only ever added to a story that exists. Adding one to a
        story that doesn't, as one deleted while a proposal naming it waited,
        or by another window, or whose file was removed from
        `.suspense/planning/` meanwhile, changes nothing: no story is made
        for it, no other story is given it, and nothing is saved. It says so
        in plain words where it was asked for, as "That story no longer
        exists, so the step wasn't added", in the theme's error colour, as
        the states say, with what was to be added kept, so it can be added
        to another story or as a new one. A step added to a story already
        sent is refused the same way, saying the story has been sent.

    layout:
        Everything in Planning is laid out on one rhythm, so it scans as a
        single list. The column has 24 pixels of padding at its top and
        sides. Each section's heading is a row 32 pixels tall: its name in
        small semibold text, its count beside it, muted, and its actions at
        its right, each a labelled button, never an icon alone; 8 pixels
        beneath it its first row. Story rows are 36 pixels tall, 2 pixels
        apart, each with 12 pixels of padding at either side, their parts in
        fixed columns, so the grips, mode pills, titles, and statuses line up
        down the whole list: the grip 16 pixels, the mode pill 72 pixels, the
        title the rest, the status and time right-aligned in a column of
        their own 96 pixels wide, then the row's buttons. Sections are 24
        pixels apart. Every row's state reads the same way, as below, and
        every label is the same small text, muted where it is secondary.

    states:
        Each part of Planning has the same few states, shown the same way
        wherever they come up, so a state is never guessed from what is
        missing.

        - Empty: a single muted line, centred in the section, saying what is missing and what to do, as "Nothing planned. Drag stories here, or press Ctrl+N.", with no illustration
        - Loading: a spinner and a short muted label of what is happening, as "Drafting stories…", in the place the result will appear, never a blank space
        - Paused: a story whose task is paused shows "Paused" as its status, in the theme's warning colour, with a small pause icon, and a "Resume" button in its row, as the PromptSending says of pausing; a sprint with any story paused says so in its heading, as "1 paused", in the same colour
        - Error: a line in the theme's error colour, saying what went wrong in plain words, with what the harness or the application reported beneath it collapsed under "Details", and a "Try again" button where trying again can help
        \\

        A story's status in its row is the same coloured label a task has,
        as the @{MessageList}'s status says, Queued, Running with its spinner
        and time, Done, Failed, Cancelled, or Paused, and a story not yet
        sent shows nothing there, so its absence means "not sent".

    drafting:
        Drafting stories shows its work in one place, a panel opened beneath

        the request box at its top, labelled "Describe what you want", and
        beneath it, while the run goes, its research: a muted line of what
        the harness is doing, as "Reading the spec…", with its spinner,
        updating as it goes, and a "Stop" button. Once it ends, the panel
        lists its proposals, as below, then "Accept all" and "Reject all"

        to decide. A run that fails shows its error, as the states say, and
        leaves the request in its box to try again; one that proposes nothing
        says so, as an empty state. Proposals are kept until each is decided,
        so closing Planning and coming back finds them as they were.

        Drafting can also be started from an open story, with "Ask agent"
        in its row's menu or the open story's footer: the request box then
        reads "What does this story need?", the run is told the story's
        title and prompt, and the panel opens beneath that story rather than
        the Backlog's heading.

    proposals:
        The agent never writes the plan itself. Its run is a Question run,
        as the @{Sandbox} says, able to read the project and change nothing,
        and Suspense data is never granted to it, so it can't touch
        `.suspense/planning/`; it only proposes, and nothing it proposes

        Each proposal is one concrete task, with a title, a prompt, and the
        mode that fits it, and says where it should go: either "New story",

        story the run was shown, the open story first, to be added to it. The
        planning prompt of the @{BakedSystemPrompts} asks for each proposal

        block that names a story that no longer exists is shown as "New
        story", with a muted note saying so.

        Each proposal is a card in the panel, in the order given: a label at
        its top, "New story" in the theme's accent or "Add to" and the
        story's title in Spec's or the story's own mode's colour; its title,
        its mode pill, and its prompt beneath, clipped at four lines with

        "Reject", reachable by Tab and labelled for a screen reader. Edit

        Its findings are a document of their own, "Research: <topic>",

        when it ran, and its state, and opening in a body tab of its own to

export ui-component AskConversation:
    pitch:
        The questions asked from the Ask tab, read as a chat: every question
        and its answer, one after another, in a pane of its own beside the
        tasks, with each new conversation clearly marked where it begins.

    description:
        While the @{ChatInput}'s Ask tab is selected, the conversation
        fills the body's Chat tab, beneath the tab bar and above the chat
        input, in place of the message list, as the @{Body} says, never
        sharing the body with it or with anything else. It goes when another
        mode's tab is selected, the message list coming back in its place,
        and comes back as it was, scrolled where it was, when Ask is
        selected again. Nothing slides as it comes and goes.

        It is drawn in the @{Theme}'s roles, on the same base surface as
        the message list. Along its top runs a header 32 pixels tall, on the
        tab bar's background with the theme's line beneath it, reading
        "Questions" at its left, with 12 pixels of padding, and at its right
        how many questions it holds, muted. Beneath it, the
        conversation spans the full width of the space it fills, from the
        body's left edge to its right, or to the right sidebar while it is
        there, its questions and answers laid out across all of it with
        only its own padding at either side, never set in a narrower column,
        centred or not, and never leaving empty space beside it. It widens
        and narrows with the body as the window or a sidebar is resized.

    conversation:
        The pane lists every question of the project, those saved with it
        and those asked since, running or finished, oldest at the top and the
        newest at the bottom, the way a chat reads. Each is a message and its
        reply. The question is shown as it was typed, not as it was compiled,
        in a box on the theme's raised surface, faintly tinted Ask's colour,
        as the @{PromptModes} colours it, with corners rounded 6 pixels,
        set against the pane's right edge and at most 80% of its width,
        wrapping within that, with anything it was sent with, attached text
        and images, listed beneath its text as the chat input lists them.
        Beneath the box, at its right, sits a small muted line with the time
        it was asked and, once it is finished, a Resend button, which asks the
        question again as the @{PromptSending} says, the new question
        coming in at the bottom.

        Its answer follows beneath it, as a chat reply rather than a task:
        against the pane's left edge, across the pane's full width, with no
        box. The answer is read as prose, not as a list of what the harness
        did.

    answers:
        While an answer is being written, its status line shows the output
        rate beside it, and once it is over, a small muted line at its foot
        gives its average output rate, as the @{MessageList}'s status says
        of a task.

        An answer is not drawn as a @{TaskTable}: it has no columns, no
        Type badges or Status labels, and no lines between rows. What is
        shown is the answer's reply text, the reply rows after the harness's
        last tool call, as the table's collapsed steps count them, rendered
        as markdown in the body's text colour, one paragraph after another,
        as a message in a chat is. Code blocks, lists, tables, and links in it
        are rendered as markdown renders them anywhere. An answer with no tool
        calls is all reply text; a finished answer with nothing to show reads
        "No answer.", muted.

        Everything the harness did before the answer, its tool calls and any
        reply text between them, is gathered into one line above the answer,
        small and muted, beside a right chevron, summing it up, as "Read 3
        files, searched twice, ran 1 command" or "Worked through 6 steps"
        where it can't be summed up by kind. Clicking it expands the steps
        in place, beneath it and above the answer, as compact muted lines,
        one per step: a tool call as its tool's name, muted, then its most
        telling argument, shortened as the @{TaskTable}'s tool calls
        are, and reply text between them as muted markdown; clicking it again
        collapses them. It starts collapsed, and stays as it was left for as
        long as the application runs. An answer whose harness did nothing
        before replying has no such line.

        While the harness works on a question, a status line takes that
        line's place: a spinner and the latest thing the harness did, muted,
        with a Stop button at its right that stops just that question,
        leaving the others running. Reply text streams in beneath it as
        prose as the harness writes it; text it goes on to follow with a tool
        call joins the steps once the call comes, so only the answer is left
        as prose. Once the question finishes, the status line becomes the
        summary line.

        A question that failed ends its answer with the error, in the
        theme's error colour, beneath whatever reply came before it. One that
        was stopped ends with "Stopped", muted. Neither is shown as a status
        in a table.

        Questions are 16 pixels apart, and a question's answer 8 pixels
        beneath it.

        Questions asked while another is still running come in at the bottom
        in the order they were asked, each answered in its own place as its
        harness goes, so answers can be filling in at once.

    suggestedPrompts:
        An answer can hand back a prompt for the user to send, as a fenced
        code block whose info string is `suspense-prompt`, followed by a
        space and the mode it is meant for, `code`, `chain`, `spec`, `ask`, or
        `freeform`, as the @{PromptModes} names them, and holding the
        prompt's text, as the card format of the @{ModeSystemPrompts}
        tells the harness. Such a block
        is never shown as a code block. It is shown in the answer, where it
        stands among the reply's markdown, as a prompt card: a box on the
        theme's raised surface, faintly tinted the mode's colour, with
        corners rounded 6 pixels, across the answer's full width. Along its
        top runs a small header, the mode's icon and name in the mode's
        colour, as "Code prompt", and beneath it the prompt's text as it was
        written, wrapped, in the body's text colour, not rendered as
        markdown.

        A card starts collapsed, its text cut to its first line, cut off with
        an ellipsis, and a chevron at the right of its header. Clicking the
        header or the chevron expands it to show the whole prompt, the
        chevron turning down, and clicking again collapses it; its buttons
        work either way, sending or copying the whole prompt. Each card
        stays as it was left for as long as the application runs, and
        expanding or collapsing one never scrolls the pane. Along its bottom, at its right, is a row of small buttons,
        4 pixels apart, wrapping onto another line where the card is too
        narrow: Copy, with a copy icon, which puts the prompt's text on the
        clipboard; Edit, with a pencil icon, as below; "Add to backlog",
        with a list icon, which adds the prompt as a story in the card's mode
        to the Planning's Backlog and reads "Added" with a check after; and
        then "Send to
        Code", "Send to Chain", and "Send to Spec", in that order, each with
        an arrow icon and in its mode's colour, as the @{PromptModes}
        colours them. The send button for the card's own mode, where it is
        one of those three, is filled in its colour, and the others are ghost
        buttons in theirs, so the one the answer meant stands out while every
        task mode is a click away. A card for `ask` or `freeform` has, before
        the three, "Ask" or "Send to Freeform", filled in that mode's colour,
        the three after it as ghosts.

        Each send button sends the prompt's text at once, in its mode, as
        though it had been written in the @{ChatInput} on that tab and
        sent, as the @{PromptSending} says, the Chain button sending it as
        a Chain prompt: a task is compiled anew, building the spec first,
        and queues while its lane is busy, and a question runs at once. It
        is sent with the Slice toggle as it stands, with nothing attached,
        and what is being written in the chat input, and attached to it, is
        left alone. The button then reads "Sent to Code", "Sent to Chain",
        "Sent to Spec", "Asked", or "Sent to Freeform", with a check, and
        keeps reading so: it never times out or resets, and it is disabled
        for good, so the prompt is never sent twice from it, however long
        after, and across restarts, kept with the question's record. The
        card's other send buttons stay as they were, so the prompt can still
        be sent to another mode, each once. The tooltip of
        each says what it does, as "Send this prompt as a Code task".

        Edit puts the prompt's text in the chat input's text input instead,
        and selects the card's mode's tab, Chain for Code and Spec selected
        together where the mode is `chain`, giving the input keyboard focus
        with the cursor at the end of the text. It never sends anything: the
        user reads, edits, and sends it as any prompt. Where the input
        already holds text, that text is set aside first as the chat input
        sets aside a prompt for editing a queued one, and comes back once the
        prompt from the card is sent or cleared, so nothing typed is lost.
        What is attached to the prompt being written stays attached. The
        button reads "Edited", with a check, for 2 seconds after.

        A block whose mode is missing or isn't one of those five is still a
        prompt card, headed "Prompt", in Ask's colour, with all three send
        buttons as ghosts, and Edit selects Chain, the tab the chat input
        starts on. While a block is
        still streaming in, its card is shown with what has come so far and
        its buttons disabled until the block closes. A block never closed by
        the end of a finished answer is a card all the same, holding what
        came. An answer may hold any number of cards, each in its place.

    askingBack:
        An answer can ask the user something back, as a fenced code block
        whose info string is `suspense-question`, holding the question on its
        first lines, and then, if the harness offers answers to pick from,
        one answer per line, each begun with a dash and a space, as a
        Markdown list item is. Such a block is never shown as a code block.
        It is shown in the answer, where it stands, as a question card: a
        box on the theme's raised surface, faintly tinted Ask's colour, with
        corners rounded 6 pixels, across the answer's full width, holding the
        question rendered as markdown, and beneath it a button per answer
        offered, in the order given, each reading that answer.

        Clicking an answer asks it at once as the next question, carrying on
        the conversation of the question it answers, as asking any question
        does, as the @{PromptSending} says, its text the card's question
        quoted as a Markdown block quote, then the answer picked on a
        paragraph of its own. The new question comes in at the bottom, as
        any does. The card then shows the answer picked as chosen, in Ask's
        colour, its other buttons muted and disabled, so each card is
        answered once. The answer picked is saved with the question whose
        answer holds the card, among the questions asked, so a card answered
        stays answered when the project is opened again. A card
        with no answers to pick from has no buttons: the user answers it by
        asking a question, as ever. While a block is still streaming in, its
        buttons are disabled until it closes.

    newConversation:
        Where a new conversation begins, it is clearly marked: above the first
        question of each conversation, the first question in the pane
        included, runs a divider across the pane's full width, a line in Ask's
        colour at either side of a label reading "New conversation", then,
        muted, the date and time its first question was asked. A question
        starts a new conversation as its saved record says, in its hidden
        anchor's newConversation, as the @{ChatInput} says; a question
        saved before that was recorded carries on the one above it, unless it
        is the first. A question asked while another was running carries on a
        copy of that conversation, as the @{HarnessIntegration} says, and
        is not marked.

        Pressing New conversation for questions puts the divider in at the
        bottom of the pane straight away, beneath the last question, reading
        "New conversation" with no time, so it is plain that the next
        question starts with no context; the time is filled in once that
        question is asked. Pressed again with nothing asked since, it adds no
        second divider.

    scrolling:
        The pane scrolls, with a @{Scrollbar}, and opens scrolled to the
        bottom, on the newest question, the first time it is shown. While it
        is at the bottom it stays locked there, following each question asked
        and each answer as it grows; scrolling up unlocks it, and scrolling
        back to the bottom locks it again. Asking a question always scrolls it
        to the bottom and locks it. When a question's answer finishes,
        however it ended, the pane scrolls so the start of that answer is at
        its top, unlocking it, so the answer is read from its beginning,
        unless the user scrolled the pane while it was answering, or another
        question is still answering beneath it, when it is left where it is. However many questions it holds, and
        however long their answers, it lays out only what is in view: each
        question, divider, summary line, and block of an answer's markdown is
        drawn as it scrolls into view, so a long conversation costs no more to show,
        scroll, or resize than a short one.

    empty:
        With no question asked yet, the pane reads "No questions yet. Ask one
        below.", muted, centred in it.

    selectingText:
        The text of any question, answer, or expanded step in the pane can be
        selected by dragging across it, as any text can. A drag that selects
        text ending within the pane shows a @{SelectionPopover} with two
        buttons, "Copy", with a copy icon, and "Attach to prompt", with a
        paperclip icon. Copy puts the selected text on the clipboard; Attach to prompt
        adds it to the prompt as an attachment. Either one clears the
        selection, and the popover closes when the pane goes.

    elsewhere:
        While another tab is selected, the questions still running stay in
        view as small rows stacked directly above the chat input's tabs, the
        newest nearest them, each showing its first line and the latest thing
        the harness did, in a column that pushes what is above it up rather

        Ask tab, the pane scrolled to that question. There is no stack while
        Ask is selected: its questions are in the pane.

    projects:

        scrolled and whether it was locked to the bottom while the
